feature_contract.goal: Preserve the complete original car-reflection appearance at normal VR cadence while reducing cubemap face-submission bursts in actual late 90/120 Hz headset frames with fail-closed original 60 Hz and desktop semantics.
feature_contract.scope_boundary: Only original Envmap_FaceCount midhook and R84 car-reflection face budget; DX11, DXVK, original wheel input/FFB, stage culling, HUD, menu, SkyGlow, per-eye optics and native resolution are unchanged.
feature_contract.special_work_evidence: Quantitative code-path performance failure: at 120 Hz the deadline is 8.333 ms, but the old fixed 18 ms threshold did not mark a 12 ms frame as late. The preexisting reflection budget permitted up to three cube faces instead of a two-face late cap. This is a deterministic, code-confirmed frame-budget overrun; Quest3/VDXR GPU p95, p99 and net FPS improvement remain unmeasured.
trace_stages: Original PC Envmap_RenderToCubeMap requests cube faces via the original EXE+0x1447E CPU hook.
R84 VRNormalizeReflectionRate computes QPC inter-frame delta, uses the stable measured cadence to classify late frames, and passes the result to ReflectionFrameBudget::Advance.
The original D3D9 game renders allocated cube faces before per-eye stereo host composition; physical GPU timing and HMD visual acceptance require later headset measurement.
subcomponents: Adaptive healthy frame cadence capture and bounded late-frame detection at 60/72/80/90/120 Hz that preserves the original >18ms safety cutoff.
Preserved original car-reflection face accumulation, frame cap, zero-rate clearing, desktop/VR-off fallback and negative invalid/reset cases.
Portable compiled C++ positive/negative test plus mandatory exact-SHA Active Windows game/host/package, Domain Isolation, Full Source Impact and HUD Inspector CI.

acceptance_items.expected_behavior: A 12ms QPC interval after stable 120Hz VR frames is classified as late and caps the original reflection submission to two cube faces; valid on-time frames preserve original update rate.

acceptance_items.behavior_area: Original graphics quality, native desktop and bad clocks
acceptance_items.expected_behavior: Default VR and desktop zero-rate original reflection semantics survive Reset, invalid elapsed counters, background pauses, 60Hz limit and recovery without introducing HUD, FFB or SkyGlow side effects.

acceptance_items.behavior_area: Exact-SHA Windows x86 game, x64 host and source scope
acceptance_items.expected_behavior: The material result and repaired C++ regression compile and pass four existing required exact-SHA DX9Ex Active, Domain, Full Source Impact and HUD Inspector gates.

diagnosis.root_cause: The reflection scheduler recognized lateness only when QPC elapsed exceeded 18ms, a 60Hz-era threshold. At 90/120Hz a 12–15ms gap can miss the XR refresh deadline while incorrectly granting the three-face on-time GPU reflection cap.
source_trace: Original Envmap_FaceCount hook receives a 60Hz-normalized reflection face budget request.
QPC frame delta passes into static lateFrame bool then ReflectionFrameBudget::Advance chooses 3 versus 2 face cap.
Original D3D9 cubemap face rendering consumes GPU time before the per-eye OpenXR compositor receives the completed game-eye textures.
alternatives_rejected: Reducing reflection texture resolution or removing reflections would change game quality rather than correct the late-frame limiter.
Changing SkyGlow, original game timers or global D3D9 Draw/Flush alters unrelated protected original rendering paths.
Using an unchecked static fixed 120Hz target would falsely classify valid 60/72/80/90Hz HMD or desktop frames.
diagnosis.runtime_limit: Local C++ test reproduces code-path timing and allocation; hardware Quest3/VDXR GPU frame-time, optical quality and actual FPS remain UNTESTED.
